name: Hahn's Bay Recreation Area (Turtle Mountain State Forest)
note: ND Forest Service campground on Lake Metigoshe in Turtle Mountain State Forest, NE of Bottineau (390 Hahn's Bay Rd). About 16 primitive drive-in sites on a grassy loop; vault toilets, picnic shelter, public boat ramp and fishing pier, access to an 8-mile paved trail. First-come, first-served, firewood included with registration; closed to camping in winter. --Claude

name: Coldwater Access
note: Missouri Department of Conservation area (79 acres). Primitive camping at MDC-designated sites (MDC lists 'Designated Camping Sites'); MDC does not map where the sites are, so this pin is the area centre on its access track (no lot mapped). No hookups, no reservations; 14-day limit in any 30. Site length not published. From Silva, take Highway 67 north approximately 9 miles, then take County Road 302 west 3 miles to the river. --Claude

name: Beall Woods State Park
note: Illinois DNR park on the Wabash River near Mount Carmel, known for its old-growth forest. 16 Class C drive-in sites, no electric or showers; pit toilets, drinking water and a dump station. First-come, no reservations; staff come round to issue permits. --Claude

name: Hennepin Canal Lock 6 Campground
note: Illinois DNR Hennepin Canal State Park designated camping location at Lock 6 near Wyanet. Primitive Class C camping (tent, RV or pop-up alike), first-come, no reservations; the site officer collects fees nightly. Pit toilet, fire pits; no water (drinking water only at the Sheffield visitor center), no hookups, no dump station. Site length not published. --Claude

name: Walker River State Recreation Area - Bighorn Campground (The Elbow)
note: Primitive campground at the Elbow on the East Walker River, a detached unit of Walker River State Recreation Area reached by 6-7 miles of graded county dirt road east off NV-338 (about 15 miles north of Bridgeport, CA). Roughly two dozen first-come, first-served gravel sites in the willows along the river, with tables, fire rings and vault toilets; no water, no hookups. Trophy trout water. 14-day limit in 30. --Claude

name: Lewis Wetzel WMA Campground
note: WV DNR campground in the 14,000-acre Lewis Wetzel Wildlife Management Area south of New Martinsville, near Jacksonburg (Wetzel County). First come first served. Trailheads for loop hikes leave from the campground. --Claude

name: Bertha Camping Area (Bluestone WMA)
note: Summers County-run primitive camping area on Bluestone Lake's east shore at the end of County Route 3/3, south of Hinton, inside Bluestone Wildlife Management Area. Sites strung along the shoreline in dirt clearings; fire rings, some tables. CAVEATS: nobody has reported what size rig fits - sites are dirt pads reached by gravel county roads, so scout before bringing a motorhome in; the area floods in high water and parts may flood more often during the ongoing Bluestone Dam work (DNR District 4, 304-256-6947, has gate-closure updates). --Claude  AWH 2026-10-11: kept, though we can't tell whether the sites suit RVs. Call (304) 466-7119 for info. --Claude

name: Mouth of Indian Creek Camping Area (Bluestone WMA)
note: The largest of the Summers County-run camping areas on Bluestone WMA, on the flats where Indian Creek meets the New River, off Mouth of Indian Creek Road near Forest Hill. Boat ramp; fire rings, some tables. CAVEATS: nobody has reported what size rig fits - sites are dirt pads reached by gravel county roads, so scout before bringing a motorhome in; the area floods in high water and parts may flood more often during the ongoing Bluestone Dam work (DNR District 4, 304-256-6947, has gate-closure updates). --Claude  AWH 2026-10-11: kept, though we can't tell whether the sites suit RVs. Call (304) 466-7119 for info. --Claude

name: Cedar Branch Camping Area (Bluestone WMA)
note: Summers County-run primitive camping area strung along the south bank of the New River at the end of Cedar Branch Road, across from Crumps Bottom, inside Bluestone Wildlife Management Area. Fire rings and some tables. CAVEATS: nobody has reported what size rig fits - sites are dirt pads reached by gravel county roads, so scout before bringing a motorhome in; the area floods in high water and parts may flood more often during the ongoing Bluestone Dam work (DNR District 4, 304-256-6947, has gate-closure updates). --Claude  AWH 2026-10-11: kept, though we can't tell whether the sites suit RVs. --Claude

name: Shanklin's Ferry Camping Area (Bluestone WMA)
note: Summers County-run primitive camping area on the New River at the end of Shanklins Ferry Road, the southernmost of the Bluestone WMA camping areas, near the Virginia line. A playground and shooting range are nearby. Fire rings and some tables. CAVEATS: nobody has reported what size rig fits - sites are dirt pads reached by gravel county roads, so scout before bringing a motorhome in; the area floods in high water and parts may flood more often during the ongoing Bluestone Dam work (DNR District 4, 304-256-6947, has gate-closure updates). --Claude  AWH 2026-10-11: kept, though we can't tell whether the sites suit RVs. --Claude

name: Coppermine Bottom Campground (DNR)
note: Primitive WA DNR campground on the Clearwater River in the Olympic Experimental State Forest, about 13 miles up the paved Hoh-Clearwater Mainline from US-101 near Queets. 11 sites (one group), vault toilet, day-use shelter, hand boat launch; no water or hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 30 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. DNR warned in 2026 of logging traffic on the access road. --Claude

name: Minnie Peterson Campground (DNR)
note: Small primitive WA DNR campground on the paved Upper Hoh Road, a mile past Willoughby Creek, on the way to Olympic National Park's Hoh Rain Forest. Nine forested sites along a creek, vault toilet, no water or hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 30 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. A cheap overflow when the park's Hoh campground is full. --Claude

name: Hoh Oxbow Campground (DNR)
note: Small primitive WA DNR campground in an oxbow of the Hoh River right off US-101 near the Hoh River bridge. Eight sites under mossy old forest, vault toilet, hand boat launch; no water or hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 30 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. Closed 2026-09-14 to 2026-10-13 for Hoh Bridge repair on US-101. --Claude

name: Cottonwood Campground (DNR, Hoh River)
note: Primitive WA DNR campground near the lower Hoh River, off Oil City Road west of US-101 (MP 177-178), the last 0.9 mile on gravel. Ten sites, vault toilet, hand boat launch; no water or hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 30 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: South Fork Hoh Campground (DNR)
note: Remote primitive WA DNR campground on the South Fork Hoh River, near the Olympic National Park boundary and the South Fork Hoh trailhead. Seven sites, shelter, vault toilet; no water or hookups. The last 7.4 miles are one-lane road, mostly gravel. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 30 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. DNR warned in 2026 of logging traffic on the access road. --Claude

name: Dragoon Creek Campground (DNR)
note: WA DNR campground on Dragoon Creek just off US-395 about 10 miles north of Spokane - one of DNR's more developed camps. 23 sites, drinking water, vault toilets, shelter, camp host; no hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 26 ft; three-day stay limit. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED for the 2026 season per DNR (checked 2026-09-29). --Claude

name: Flodelle Creek Campground (DNR)
note: Small WA DNR campground among western larch on Flodelle Creek in the Little Pend Oreille forest east of Colville, near the Tacoma Divide ORV trails. Eight sites, drinking water, vault toilet; no hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 26 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED since 2025-09-08 along with its access road after the Tacoma Creek Fire; still listed closed on 2026-09-29. --Claude

name: Starvation Lake Campground (DNR)
note: WA DNR campground on 26-acre Starvation Lake near the Little Pend Oreille Wildlife Refuge, 10.5 miles east of Colville off SR-20. 14 sites - only a few suit RVs - vault toilets, fishing dock, camp host; no water or hookups. Shallow lake popular with ospreys and bald eagles. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 26 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Douglas Falls Grange Park Campground (DNR)
note: WA DNR campground in the 120-acre Douglas Falls Grange Park, about 6 miles north of Colville, beside Mill Creek and its 60-foot waterfall. 13 sites, vault toilets, shelter, ball field, camp host; no hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 26 ft. The foot bridge was closed in 2026. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Sherry Creek Campground (DNR)
note: WA DNR campground in mixed conifer forest near the Little Pend Oreille Lakes, just off SR-20 about 24 miles east of Colville, at the Little Pend Oreille ORV trail system - expect riders. Ten sites plus three group sites, vault toilets, shelter, ORV ramp, camp host; no water or hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 35 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Skookum Creek Campground (DNR)
note: WA DNR campground along Skookum Creek east of the Pend Oreille River at Usk, near the Idaho line - a local favorite. Ten wooded sites, drinking water, vault toilets, shelter, camp host; no hookups. The last 0.4 mile is one-lane gravel. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 28 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Ahtanum Campground (DNR)
note: The most accessible WA DNR campground in the Ahtanum State Forest west of Yakima, on the North Fork of Ahtanum Creek near the end of the paved road (via Ahtanum Road and Middle Fork Road from Tampico). 12 sites, vault toilets, camp host; no potable water in 2026 (broken water line) and no hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 32 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. DNR planned prescribed burns in the area 2026-09-14 to 10-15. --Claude

name: Ahtanum Meadows Campground (DNR)
note: Small WA DNR campground in the Ahtanum State Forest west of Yakima, just before Ahtanum Campground, and the winter trailhead for 67 miles of groomed snowmobile trails. Only a couple of drive-in overnight sites (four others are walk-in, day use only), vault toilets; no potable water in 2026 and no hookups. DNR says drive-in sites take trailers up to about 32 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Clover Flats Campground (DNR)
note: High WA DNR campground (about 6,300 ft) at the west end of the Middle Fork Road in the Ahtanum State Forest west of Yakima, reached by 9.2 miles of one-lane gravel past Ahtanum Camp; near the Goat Rocks Wilderness views. Nine sites, drinking water, vault toilet; no hookups. Horses allowed but no highlines. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 28 ft; summer only in practice. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Tree Phones Campground (DNR)
note: Popular WA DNR campground near Darland Mountain in the Ahtanum State Forest west of Yakima, 5.8 miles past Ahtanum Camp on one-lane gravel (A-2000). Two camping areas: horse camping on the north side of the road, general camping on the south. Drinking water, vault toilets, hitching posts; no hookups. Trailhead for the 23-mile Grey Rock Trail; busy in hunting season. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 35 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Bird Creek Campground (DNR)
note: Small WA DNR campground on the east side of Mount Adams above Glenwood, a base for the area's lava tubes and volcanic geology. Nine forested sites, vault toilets; no water or hookups. Reached on gravel DNR roads (K-3000, S-4000, K-4000) from Glenwood. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 32 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Island Camp (DNR)
note: Small WA DNR campground along Bird Creek on the east side of Mount Adams, near the lava tubes, a few miles beyond Bird Creek Campground. Six sites, shelter, vault toilet, plus a rentable cabin; no water or hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to about 32 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED as of 2026-09-29: DNR lists the campground closed, with hazard-tree and footbridge work at the cabin/day-use area through about 2026-10-01. --Claude

name: Cold Creek Campground (DNR, Yacolt Burn)
note: Small WA DNR campground in the Yacolt Burn State Forest northeast of Vancouver, at the hub of 35 miles of non-motorized trails (Bells Mountain Trail). Eight sites, vault toilet, shelter, camp host; no water or hookups. DNR says it takes trailers up to 25 ft. Open Thursday to Monday only (closed Monday afternoon to Thursday morning) through October 15. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Winston Creek Campground (DNR)
note: Forested streamside WA DNR campground in the Winston Creek forest block south of Mossyrock and Mayfield Lake, popular in elk season. 10-11 sites, vault toilets, camp host; no water or hookups. DNR says sites take trailers up to 25 ft. Closed mid-December to mid-May. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Camp Spilman (DNR)
note: Year-round WA DNR campground in the Tahuya State Forest west of Belfair, on the edge of 200+ miles of multi-use trails - mostly ORV, so expect motorbikes. Ten sites, vault toilet; no water or hookups. DNR says sites take RVs up to about 30 ft. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Leader Lake Campground (DNR)
note: WA DNR campground around Leader Lake, 0.4 mile up a paved one-lane road off SR-20 about 8 miles west of Okanogan. About 19 mostly open sites along the shore on both sides of the lake, vault toilets, boat launch; no water or hookups. Popular for bass, crappie and trout. Most sites suit rigs under about 25 ft (reports of up to 35 ft in the best spots). First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. The south-side campground and dam were closed for repaving July-September 2026; the north side stayed open. --Claude

name: Palmer Lake Campground (DNR)
note: Small roadside WA DNR campground on the shore of 2,100-acre Palmer Lake, 8.5 miles north of Loomis on the paved Loomis-Oroville Road, among orchards and mountains near the Canadian border. Six or seven open gravel sites right at the water, vault toilet, hand boat launch; no water or hookups. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. In September 2026 DNR warned it could close as the Sinlahekin Fire spread north of Loomis - check before going. --Claude

name: Toats Coulee Campground (DNR)
note: Small WA DNR campground in two areas (upper and lower) along Toats Coulee creek among glacier-smoothed boulders, 5.5 miles up the steep, potholed paved Toats Coulee Road from Loomis. Nine sites, vault toilets; no water or hookups. Sites are short (a 28-ft trailer is the longest reported). First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED as of 2026-09-29: the whole Loomis State Forest was closed for the Sinlahekin Fire. --Claude
